purpose: Known source dependence and non-independence exclusions for candidate discovery. These rules do not exhaust all textual relationships.

work_families.rationale: The Gītā is embedded in the Mahābhārata tradition, and cross-volume matches can reflect repeated wording or internal doublets rather than independent evidence.

pair_rules.rationale: The anthology reproduces Müller's Dhammapada translation.
The anthology contains material overlapping Sale's Qur'an translation.
Extended King James wording occurs in the Book of Mormon; lexical overlap is not independent evidence.
The modern compilation draws on Biblical and later Jewish sources and cannot automatically corroborate them independently.
Historical translations and commentary may share ancient sources or modern wording; independence is not established.
The secondary synthesis retells related K'iche' material and is not an independent witness.
The secondary work reproduces or closely adapts tales from Strange Stories from a Chinese Studio.
The secondary Celtic synthesis retells Mabinogion narratives and is not an independent witness.
The collections contain closely shared Tinguian tale texts and cannot be assumed independent.
The secondary synthesis retells Cherokee material attested in the ethnographic collection.
The secondary synthesis retells Haudenosaunee material attested in the ethnographic collection.
The collections contain closely related versions of the same Japanese tales.
The historical commentary directly quotes the King James Bible.
The historical translation and commentary directly quotes Biblical passages.
Related Norse literary material cannot be assumed to provide independent attestation.
